description: Somos estudiantes llenos de vocación por aprender. Hemos participado en proyectos de robótica, en la radio escolar y en el desarrollo de M1K1U, una estación meteorológica escolar. Nos motiva la ciencia, la exploración espacial y la innovación tecnológica para aportar soluciones que impulsen el conocimiento y el desarrollo sostenible.
summary:
We have created an educational 3D video game in which children go from being mere spectators to becoming explorers of Mars. Accompanied by Minibot, Bitbot, and Atlas, they take on eight missions inspired by real-life challenges on the planet—ranging from dust storms to the mechanics of solar energy. 

Each mission is developed based on research and scientific resources from NASA. Furthermore, the game incorporates an approach rooted in child psychology, tailoring its challenges and experiences to the way children learn and discover the world around them.
details:
We developed a 3D educational video game. Children (aged 7 to 12) can play the video game directly in the browser. It's not that they watch a mission, but rather they live the mission. It consists of 8 interconnected missions. In this way, they become an astronaut. They must explore real craters and collect samples. The children are the ones who make the decisions that determine the success or failure of the mission.

The best aspect of Ares 01 is that we have removed easy mode. There is no easy and free solution (like in a real NASA mission). For example, do I use my last battery to analyze an incredible sample or do I make sure I have oxygen for the Martian night? This is where real learning happens.

Everything is real. This is our main strong point. All elements (dust storms, radiation alerts, or terrain configuration) are based on real and open data from NASA. For real space weather we use the DONKI API. For the exact topography of Mars we use Mars Trek. And the real effect on human health we get from the OSDR repository. So, when children protect themselves from radiation in the game, they are facing a phenomenon that NASA is currently monitoring.

The impact is transformative. We go from passive admiration to active training. Children who play Ares 01 go from "dreaming" to thinking like astronauts. They develop critical thinking, resource management, and resilience. Today we are creating the mindset of the crew that will take humanity to Mars.

We do it to win and to reach everyone. We have used open and accessible web technologies. We use HTML and JavaScript. The three.jss library is what we have used for the entire 3D environment (rendering and interaction). In this way we have achieved an immersive experience optimized in WebGL. In this way any judge, teacher, or child in the world can play the video game (with just a link).

With Ares 01 we have the tool that NASA needs for the next generation to truly learn, and it was also made from extensive research into a child's mind so that they learn faster.
